Poor excuse for a Japanese restaurant
Dec 2019 • Couples
On a busy street corner amongst many Japanese catering restaurants, you feel welcomed and gaily greeted when you step in the door. The beer ladies greet you, one wearing a Sapporo dress and one wearing Tiger. The beer comes out quickly, but then the service and food quality becomes a real disappointment. People around us seemed to enjoy the hot pot with top ramen noodles, but my dish of short ribs on a hot plate was not short ribs at all. It was the toughest 8 pieces of beef I have ever been served, even in SE Asia where beef is not expected to be great. In fact, chew as I might, I ended up swallowing the pieces whole. The sushi roll was redeeming, but my wife waited and waited for her chicken teriyaki, while tables around us got served and meals eaten. And when finally served 1/2 hour later, and after a few reminders, the chicken that arrived was tough. How can chicken teriyaki be tough? It’s not a hard dish to make. The manager tried to explain this was a difficult dish to make, thus it took so long. I give up. When looking for a respectable Japanese restaurant along this busy street, there are many to choose from, so don’t choose this one!
